member.name: T:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker
member.summary: Checks a PDF document for accessibility compliance against PDF/UA and WCAG 2.2 requirements. Returns a report of compliant and non-compliant features.
member.remarks:
This checker inspects the in-memory ObviousPDF document model before serialization. It does not parse raw PDF bytes.
Based on: - ISO 14289-1 (PDF/UA-1) requirements - ISO 32000 §14.7, §14.8, §14.9 - WCAG 2.2 success criteria relevant to PDF

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.Check(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument)
member.summary: Runs all accessibility checks on the given document.

member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1: Document language shall be specified. WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.1: Language of Page.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckMarkInfo(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1: The document shall be marked (MarkInfo/Marked = true).

member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1: A structure tree shall be present with a Document root.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckDisplayDocTitle(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2: The viewer should display the document title rather than the filename. Checks that DisplayDocTitle is enabled.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckDocumentTitle(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1: Document title should be present and meaningful. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2: Page Titled.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckStructureElements(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Recursively checks structure elements for specific requirements.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFigureBBox(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.3, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1: All Figure structure elements should have a /BBox layout attribute so assistive technology can locate the figure on the page.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPageTabOrder(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA: Pages with tagged content should have /Tabs /S for logical tab order. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3: Focus Order.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckReadingOrder(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary:
PDF/UA §7.2, ISO 32000 §14.8.4.2: The structure tree shall reflect the logical reading order of the document. Content items should be present in the tree and all non-artifact content should be tagged.
The reading order is defined by the depth-first traversal of the structure tree's children. Assistive technologies present content in this order regardless of visual placement on the page.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CollectHeadingLevels(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32})
member.summary: Collects heading levels in reading order (depth-first traversal). H1=1, H2=2, ..., H6=6, H=0 (generic).

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckTableStructureDetails(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Performs detailed table structure checks per §14.8.4.8 and PDF/UA §7.5: - TH cells should have /Scope - Complex tables (multiple TH per row/column) should have /Headers on TD - Table hierarchy validation (Table → THead/TBody/TFoot/TR → TH/TD)

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.ValidateTableHierarchy(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement)
member.summary: Validates the hierarchy of a table element: direct children must be TR, THead, TBody, TFoot, or Caption; row children must be TH or TD.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.ValidateTableRow(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement)
member.summary: Validates that a TR element contains only TH or TD children.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CollectElementsByType(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.StructureType,System.Collections.Generic.List{ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement})
member.summary: Recursively collects all elements of a given type in the subtree.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckCompleteTagging(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.2: In a tagged PDF, all renderable content on every page shall be either tagged (inside a marked content sequence linked to the structure tree) or explicitly marked as an artifact. Content that is neither tagged nor artifact is invisible to assistive technologies.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckNonFigureIllustrationAltText(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.3, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1: All illustration structure elements (not just Figure — also Formula when used standalone) shall have alternative text (/Alt) so screen readers can describe them.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFirstHeadingIsH1(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.4.2, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1: The first heading in logical reading order shall be H1. Starting the document with a lower-level heading (H2–H6) indicates a broken heading hierarchy that confuses assistive technologies.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPronunciationHints(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 32000-2 §14.9.6: When pronunciation hints (/Phoneme) are used, they should specify a /PhoneticAlphabet so screen readers know how to interpret the transcription. Reports on usage of pronunciation hints.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CollectPronunciationStats(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively collects pronunciation hint statistics from the structure tree.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckLanguageOfParts(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.2 (Language of Parts, Level AA): When portions of a document are in a different language from the document-level /Lang, each such portion's structure element should carry its own /Lang attribute so screen readers switch voice/language automatically.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CountElementLanguages(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively counts non-root structure elements that have a Language set. Also validates BCP 47 format on each language override.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.IsValidBcp47Tag(System.String)
member.summary: Validates whether a string is a valid BCP 47 language tag per RFC 5646. Checks the format: primary language subtag (2-3 alpha) followed by optional subtags separated by hyphens.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckDefinitionListStructure(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.3 (Unusual Words, Level AAA): Definition lists (/L with /LI → /Lbl + /LBody) can serve as glossaries for unusual words or jargon. This advisory check reports the presence of list structures that may function as definition lists.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckReadingLevelSupport(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.5 (Reading Level, Level AAA): When the document is fully tagged with headings, sections, and language attributes, it supports supplemental content strategies. This advisory check notes whether the document's structural richness aids readability.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckReadingLevelIndicators(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Boolean@,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Checks for indicators of structural richness (headings and sections).

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckLinkStructure(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.18, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.4: Link annotations should be associated with /Link structure elements so that screen readers can announce the link purpose.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckArtifactUsage(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.1, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1: In a tagged document, all content should be either tagged (inside BMC/BDC structure) or explicitly marked as an artifact. This check looks for the presence of artifact marking to encourage its use for page numbers, headers/footers, etc.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckArtifactedTextInPageBody(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary:
PAC quality warning: text in the page body that is marked as an artifact is often a sign that meaningful labels or instructions have been hidden from assistive technologies.
Currently flagged:
Layout text artifacts — text with /Type /Layout is suspicious because the Layout artifact type is intended for decorative visual elements (ruling lines, background colours), not readable text. PAC reports these as "The page body contains marked content that contains text and is tagged as an artifact."
Pagination artifacts (page numbers, headers, footers) are not flagged because they are legitimate page furniture per ISO 32000 §14.8.2.2.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.IsArtifactedTextInPageBody(ObviousPDF.ArtifactTextEntry)
member.summary:
Returns if the artifact text entry is likely to be flagged by PAC as "artifacted content on page body":
Layout-type text artifacts (text should not use the Layout artifact type).

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFormFieldAccessibility(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.18, WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2: Every form field should have an accessible name (/TU tooltip) and be connected to a /Form structure element via OBJR.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFormStructurePlacement(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 32000-2 Annex L and PDF/UA require /Form structure elements to be nested in semantically appropriate context. A /Form element directly under the /Document root is flagged by PAC as a parsing warning ("Possibly inappropriate use of a Form structure element").

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFontEmbedding(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.21: All fonts shall be embedded. Standard (Type 1) fonts are not embedded and must not be used alone in a PDF/UA document. This check reports on the use of standard vs. embedded fonts.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckContrastWarnings(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum), SC 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast): When text uses a known foreground colour, check the contrast ratio against a white background and warn if it falls below the AA threshold for normal text (4.5:1).

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPdf20VersionConsistency(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2: When the document uses PDF 2.0 features, the PDF version should be 2.0 or auto-detected as such. Warns if the explicit version is set below 2.0 but 2.0 features are present.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckMetadataCompleteness(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2, SC 2.4.5: Document metadata should be complete to support discoverability. Checks title (already done elsewhere), author, subject, and keywords.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckNoteStructure(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1: /Note structure elements should be children of block-level elements and should have a /NoteType attribute.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.IsBlockLevelOrGrouping(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.StructureType)
member.summary: Returns true if the given structure type is a block-level or grouping element.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckExpansionUsage(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.4 (Abbreviations, AAA): When /E (Expansion) entries are used in the structure tree, reports their presence. This is an advisory check — the absence of expansions is not a failure, but their presence demonstrates good practice.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CountExpansions(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively counts structure elements that have an Expansion value.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckRoleMappings(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2: When custom structure types are used, a RoleMap must map them to standard types so assistive technology understands the semantics.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CountCustomTypes(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively counts structure elements that use a custom type name.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPdfUaIdentifier(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 14289-1 §6.7.11: PDF/UA-conforming files shall include pdfuaid:part in the XMP metadata. This check recommends enabling the PDF/UA identifier when tagged PDF features are used.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckNamespaceDeclarations(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 32000-2 §14.7.4: PDF 2.0 documents should declare the standard structure namespace on the StructTreeRoot via /Namespaces. This ensures validators interpret structure types correctly per Annex L.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.HasPdf20StructTypes(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement)
member.summary: Checks whether any element in the tree uses a PDF 2.0 structure type.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.ComparePdfVersionStrings(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Compares two PDF version strings (e.g. "1.7", "2.0").

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckRubyStructure(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 32000-2 §14.8.4.4.5: Ruby annotations should have the correct child hierarchy (Ruby → RB + RT, optionally with RP). Reports on the presence and correctness of ruby/warichu annotation structures.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckTableOfContents(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 32000 §14.8.4.3.2, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.5: When a /TOC structure element is present, it should contain /TOCI children. Reports on the presence and correctness of table-of-contents structures.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckOptionalContentAccessibility(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: §8.11, §14.8, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1: When content is placed in optional content groups (layers), it should still be tagged in the structure tree. Warns if OCG-associated structure elements are missing.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CountOcgAssociations(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively counts structure elements associated with an OCG.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPdfUa2Requirements(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 14289-2: PDF/UA-2 requirements include BBox on all illustration elements (not just Figure — also Formula), namespace declarations, and /AF on structure elements for alternative representations.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckAnnexLNesting(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Validates basic Annex L parent-child nesting rules for PDF 2.0 structure types. Sets to true if any invalid nesting is detected.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckUniqueStructureIds(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.1 (Parsing, Level A): Structure element IDs must be unique within the document. Duplicate /ID values confuse assistive technologies that use them for table header associations and cross-references.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CollectStructureIds(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: Recursively collects all non-null /ID values from the structure tree.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckLinkAnnotationNames(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value, Level A), PDF/UA §7.18: Link annotations should have an accessible name — either via /Contents on the annotation or associated link text in the /Link structure element. A link with no descriptive text forces screen readers to read the raw URI.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckHeadingContent(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value, Level A): Heading structure elements (H1–H6) should contain content items so assistive technology can announce the heading text. An empty heading element has a role but no accessible name.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckHeadingsHaveContent(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Int32@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Recursively counts headings and those that have content items or children with content.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFormFieldRequiredIndication(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages, Level AA): When form fields are marked as required (/Ff bit 2), the tooltip (/TU) should indicate the required status so screen readers can announce it without the user needing to submit the form first.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckAnnotationContents(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.18.1: Any annotation that does not have a /Contents key shall have an alternative description. For non-link annotations (Text, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly, StrikeOut, FreeText, Stamp), the /Contents entry must be present and non-empty.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckAnnotationTabOrder(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.18.3: Every page that contains annotations shall have /Tabs /S in its page dictionary so that tab order follows the structure tree. In the ObviousPDF model, /Tabs /S is written when a page has tagged content (MarkedContentElements). A page with annotations but no tagged content violates this requirement.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckEmbeddedFileDescriptions(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.11: The file specification dictionary for an embedded file should contain the /Desc key. This check verifies that all associated files (document-level and page-level) have a non-empty Description.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckToUnicodeCMap(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: PDF/UA §7.21.7: The font dictionary of all fonts shall include a ToUnicode CMap that maps character codes to Unicode values for at least all referenced glyphs. This check verifies that every embedded font glyph used in the document has a Unicode mapping.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckMathMLWellFormedness(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 14289-2 §8.2.5.29.1: When an associated file is used to provide a representation of a Formula in presentation MathML, the MathML content shall be well-formed XML.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckNamespaceRoleMappingCompleteness(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: ISO 14289-2 §8.2.4: All structure elements shall belong to, or be role mapped to, the PDF 1.7, PDF 2.0, or MathML namespaces. Custom structure types must have role mappings to standard types.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CollectUnmappedCustomTypes(ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.StructureType},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: Recursively collects custom type names that have no entry in the document's role-mapping dictionary.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckListStructure(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary:
ISO 14289-1 §7.6, Matterhorn 16-001 to 16-003: List structures shall follow the hierarchy L → LI → (Lbl + LBody). Validates:
/L elements must have at least one /LI child
/LI elements must have at least /LBody; /Lbl is optional
/Lbl and /LBody must not appear outside /LI

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckDocumentOutline(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 27-001, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.5: When a document has heading structure elements and multiple logical sections, an outline (bookmarks) should be present. If outline items exist, their titles should be non-empty.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckTableCaptions(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 15-005, ISO 14289-1 §7.5: Data tables benefit from a /Caption child element so screen readers can announce the table's purpose. Advisory: flags tables with more than 2 rows that lack a Caption child.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckTableSpanAttributes(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 15-006/007, ISO 32000 §14.8.4.8: RowSpan and ColSpan layout attributes on TH/TD cells must be within valid bounds for the table.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckPuaCodepoints(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 10-001, ISO 14289-1 §7.21.4: Characters mapped to Unicode Private Use Area codepoints (U+E000–U+F8FF, U+F0000–U+FFFFD, U+100000–U+10FFFD) shall have /ActualText set on the containing structure element so assistive technology can provide correct text.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckFullAnnexLNesting(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary:
ISO 32000-2 Annex L, ISO 14289-2 §8.2.4: Validates block/inline nesting rules beyond Ruby/Warichu/TOCI. Checks:
P and heading elements cannot contain block-level children
Span cannot contain block-level elements
Lbl and LBody only inside LI
Caption must be first or last child of its parent

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckActualTextPlacement(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 09-003, ISO 32000 §14.9.4: /ActualText on container elements (Sect, Div, Part, Art) overrides all descendant content — this is rarely correct and can suppress reading order. Warns if ActualText is set on grouping elements that have children.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckAccessibilityPermissions(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 26-001/002, ISO 32000 §7.6.4: If the document is encrypted, the accessibility permission flags must allow content extraction for assistive technology.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckDecorativeFigureConsistency(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 13-003, ISO 14289-1 §7.3: A /Figure element with empty or whitespace-only AltText is flagged — decorative images should be artifacts, not Figure structure elements.

member.name: M:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityChecker.CheckOcgDefaultVisibility(ObviousPDF.PdfDocument,ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfAccessibilityReport)
member.summary: Matterhorn 20-002, ISO 32000 §8.11.4: When an OCG has a default OFF state, content associated with it may be invisible to users even though the structure tree references it.

member.name: T:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfArtifactType
member.summary: Specifies the type of artifact in a tagged PDF (ISO 32000 §14.8.2.2, Table 396). Artifacts are content that is not part of the logical structure of the document and should be ignored by assistive technologies.

member.name: F:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfArtifactType.Pagination
member.summary: Pagination artifact — page numbers, running headers/footers, and similar content that repeats across pages.

member.name: F:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfArtifactType.Layout
member.summary: Layout artifact — ruling lines, background colours, and other decorative visual elements used for layout purposes.

member.name: F:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfArtifactType.Page
member.summary: Page artifact — content that describes the page itself rather than its content, such as cut marks or colour bars.

member.summary:
Computes WCAG 2.2 colour contrast ratios between foreground and background colours, and checks whether the resulting ratio satisfies Level AA or AAA thresholds (WCAG SC 1.4.3, SC 1.4.6, SC 1.4.11).
The contrast ratio is calculated using the relative luminance formula defined in WCAG 2.2 §1.4.3: ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) where L1 is the lighter colour and L2 is the darker colour.
Relative luminance is calculated from linearised sRGB values per WCAG 2.2 relative luminance.

member.name: T:ObviousPDF.Accessibility.PdfStructureElement
member.summary:
Represents a node in the PDF structure tree (ISO 32000 §14.7.2). Structure elements form a tree that describes the logical structure of the document's content for accessibility.
The order of children in the structure tree defines the logical reading order of the document (§14.8.4.2). Assistive technologies such as screen readers present content in the order defined by the structure tree, not the visual placement order on the page.
Use to append children in reading order. Use to insert at a specific position, to reposition an existing child, or to detach a child from this element.

Writes a linearized (web-optimized) PDF file following the structure defined in ISO 32000 Annex F.
A linearized PDF is organized so that the first page can be displayed as soon as the first portion of the file has been received, without waiting for the entire file to download. The file structure is:
Header and linearization parameter dictionary (§F.2)
First-page cross-reference table and trailer (§F.3.1)
Document catalog and first-page objects (§F.3.2)
Primary hint stream (§F.3.3)
Remaining pages' objects (§F.3.4)
Main cross-reference table and trailer for the rest (§F.3.5)
Linearization is a two-pass process: the document is first serialized to determine byte offsets and sizes, then the linearization dictionary and hint tables are patched with the actual values.

member.summary:
Gets or sets the explicit PDF version written in the file header (e.g. "2.0" for %PDF-2.0). When null the version is inferred automatically from the features used:
1.5 — cross-reference streams or object streams
2.0 — document parts (§14.12), associated files (§14.13), THead/TBody/TFoot structure types (§14.8.4.8), pronunciation hints (§14.9.6), or AES-256 encryption
Setting this property acts as a minimum floor. If the features used require a higher version than the value set here, the higher version is written. For example, setting "1.7" while using document parts still produces %PDF-2.0.

member.summary:

XMP metadata with pdfaid:part and pdfaid:conformance
An OutputIntent dictionary with an sRGB ICC profile
Full PDF/A compliance also requires embedded fonts and (for Level A) tagged PDF. These are the caller's responsibility.

member.name: P:ObviousPDF.PdfDocument.PdfUaConformance
member.summary:
Gets or sets the PDF/UA conformance level (ISO 14289). When set to , the XMP metadata includes pdfuaid:part = 1 so validators (e.g., PAC) can identify the document as claiming PDF/UA conformance.
Declaring PDF/UA conformance also requires a fully tagged document with proper structure, alt text on figures, and all other PDF/UA requirements.

member.name: P:ObviousPDF.PdfDocument.UseCrossReferenceStreams
member.summary:
Gets or sets whether the document uses cross-reference streams (ISO 32000 §7.5.8) instead of the traditional cross-reference table (§7.5.4).
Cross-reference streams encode xref entries in a compact binary format within a FlateDecode-compressed stream object, significantly reducing file overhead for large documents. This format was introduced in PDF 1.5 and is recommended for modern PDF files.
When enabled, the PDF version header is set to %PDF-1.5 and the traditional xref table and trailer dictionary are replaced by a single /Type /XRef stream object whose dictionary serves as the trailer.
This property is automatically set to true when is enabled, since object streams require cross-reference streams for Type 2 entries.

member.name: P:ObviousPDF.PdfDocument.UseObjectStreams
member.summary:
Gets or sets whether the document packs non-stream indirect objects into object streams (ISO 32000 §7.5.7).
An object stream is a stream object (/Type /ObjStm) that stores multiple non-stream objects in a single FlateDecode-compressed stream, significantly reducing file size for object-heavy documents. The format was introduced in PDF 1.5.
Object streams require cross-reference streams (§7.5.8) because compressed objects are referenced via Type 2 cross-reference entries. When this property is set to true, is implicitly enabled.
Only non-stream objects with generation number 0 are eligible for packing into object streams. Stream objects, the encryption dictionary, and the cross-reference stream itself are always written as standalone indirect objects.

member.name: P:ObviousPDF.PdfDocument.Encryption
member.summary:
Gets or sets the encryption configuration for the document (ISO 32000 §7.6). When set, all strings and streams in the PDF are encrypted using the specified algorithm and passwords. The encryption dictionary is written to the trailer.
Supported algorithms:
— AES-128 (V=4, R=4), compatible with Acrobat 7+.
— AES-256 (V=5, R=6), PDF 2.0, Acrobat X+.

member.name: P:ObviousPDF.PdfDocument.Linearize
member.summary:
Gets or sets whether the document is linearized for fast web view (ISO 32000 Annex F).
A linearized PDF reorganizes the file so that the first page can be displayed before the entire file has been downloaded. The file begins with a linearization parameter dictionary, followed by the first-page cross-reference table and first-page objects. Remaining pages and a primary hint stream follow.
Linearization is incompatible with object streams, cross-reference streams, and encryption. If any of those are enabled, is silently ignored during . Linearization is also skipped when signing via .

member.name: T:ObviousPDF.PdfXmpMetadata
member.summary:
Builds an XMP metadata stream (ISO 32000 §14.3.2) for embedding in the document catalog. XMP (Extensible Metadata Platform, ISO 16684-1) is the standard metadata format for PDF 2.0 and is required for PDF/A conformance.
The XMP packet is a well-formed XML document using the Adobe XMP schemas:
dc: — Dublin Core (title, creator/author, subject, description)
xmp: — XMP Basic (CreatorTool, CreateDate, ModifyDate)
pdf: — Adobe PDF (Producer, Keywords)
xmpMM: — XMP Media Management (DocumentID, InstanceID)
The metadata stream dictionary includes /Type /Metadata, /Subtype /XML, and the stream data is uncompressed UTF-8 XML per ISO 32000 §14.3.2 — metadata streams shall not be encrypted or compressed so that external tools can read them without decrypting the PDF.
